html:
SMTO-EXE-0104 — Looking at the screen took too long

GUID: 4405be7a-4f1d-5c63-80ca-e360ae54a15e
Slug: screen-timeout
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO gave up after 15 seconds because the computer didn't finish capturing its screen in time. No screenshot or screen text from this attempt was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer) is awake, unlocked and showing a signed-in desktop. A sleeping or locked screen can keep the capture from finishing in time.
  2. Ask SMTO to capture just one window or a smaller area instead of the whole screen. Smaller captures finish faster, so they fit inside the 15-second limit.

What success looks like

  • The new request finishes within a few seconds and the task shows the screenshot or screen text.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway, saying which screen or window you asked for. Don't try to get around the computer's privacy or screen recording settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A screen operation reached its 15-second deadline before a complete observation was confirmed; the native worker was terminated and nothing was published.

What this means

  • A screen checkpoint reached the operation's fifteen-second deadline before a complete observation was confirmed; the existing worker boundary terminates and reaps its owned subprocess. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • A screen checkpoint reached the operation's fifteen-second deadline before a complete observation was confirmed; the existing worker boundary terminates and reaps its owned subprocess.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect session/backend readiness and requested work, separating native observation timeout from the OCR-specific limit.

How to fix it

  • Check that the Gateway host has an awake, unlocked interactive desktop and review the screen worker messages in the Gateway log. Request a narrower target (one window or a region) so capture, encoding and OCR finish within TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 15 (src/gateway_core/screen_contract.py).
  • Check the selected desktop session and request a smaller region. Native workers are stopped at the fifteen-second operation deadline.

Retry and execution caution

  • Check the selected desktop session and request a smaller region. Native workers are stopped at the fifteen-second operation deadline.

How to verify the fix

  • The original worker is settled and an appropriately scoped explicit observation completes within its deadline.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
